# Results (auto-generated by `train.py`, seed 42)

## Data
| Corpus | test | train | val |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| ravdess | 240 | 960 | 240 |

RAVDESS is split **by actor** (train / validation / test actors never overlap, gender-balanced). TESS has only two speakers, so its split is
by utterance and therefore speaker-dependent: treat TESS numbers as optimistic.

## Model comparison
Models are selected on the **validation speakers**; the test speakers are used once, for reporting.

| Model | Val acc | Val macro-F1 | Test acc | Test macro-F1 |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Logistic Regression | 0.45 | 0.468 | 0.438 | 0.447 |
| SVM (RBF) | 0.517 | 0.495 | 0.533 | 0.516 |
| Random Forest | 0.467 | 0.453 | 0.475 | 0.464 |

**Selected model:** SVM (RBF)

## Why speaker-independent evaluation matters
Same model type (SVM (RBF)), same RAVDESS data:

| Evaluation | Accuracy | Macro-F1 |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| Random utterance split (same actors in train and test, **leaky**) | 0.675 | 0.652 |
| Speaker-independent (unseen actors, **honest**) | 0.533 | 0.516 |
